bull.b: FDA clearance to start a registrational Phase III and RMAT status materially de-risks OCU410’s development path. Over 2–6 months this supports accelerated regulatory engagement, increases the probability of timely BLA filing/priority review, and strengthens the program’s attractiveness to partners and payers.

Completed PPQ batches indicate CMC and scale-up risk is substantially reduced ahead of potential approvals. This durable readiness shortens commercialization lead time, lowers launch execution uncertainty and makes near-term partnerships or regional launches more feasible if clinical readouts succeed.

A substantial convertible-note raise that funds operations into 2028 provides durable financing visibility to advance three late-stage programs and file BLAs. Over multiple quarters this reduces near-term liquidity risk, allows completion of pivotal trials and regulatory submissions without immediate dilutive equity raises.

bear.b: A negative equity position is a persistent structural weakness that constrains financial flexibility and creditor confidence. Over the coming months it increases refinancing complexity, limits access to non-dilutive capital, and raises the probability that future financing terms will be more costly or dilutive.

Sustained negative operating and free cash flow means the business cannot self-fund development. Even with current runway, persistent burn over multiple quarters forces reliance on external capital or milestone monetization, amplifying execution risk if trial timelines slip or commercialization is delayed.

Reliance on contingent financing (PRV monetization, warrant exercise, authorized share increases) signals ongoing dilution risk. Structurally, this can alter capital structure, reduce existing holders' stakes, and complicate long-term incentive alignment if executed repeatedly to fund clinical and commercial activities.
